steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Point: Don't just write about one poem then the other. Weave them together - compare as you go. | Why Alternating Works: Examiners can see you're comparing throughout. It's easier to track similarities and differences. You cover both poems equally. | Top Tip: Comparison questions are typically worth 30 marks (AO1/AO2/AO3). Spend 45 minutes total: 5 mins planning your comparison points, 35 mins writing, 5 mins checking. Every paragraph must reference both poems — if you write a full paragraph on only one poem, you have already lost marks.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: What's the difference between alternating and integrated comparison? | Name three elements you should compare between poems. | Why should you include both similarities and differences?
